newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal minority govt safe in a budget vote.
newsitem.headline: Portugal minority govt safe in a budget vote.

text.p: The leader of Portugal's main opposition party said that he would not allow the minority Socialist government to fall over the 1997 budget, which is due to be debated soon in parliament.

Social Democrat Party (PSD) leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa told Reuters that his party opposed fresh elections before 1998 at the earliest. It would abstain in parliament if the government turned the budget into a confidence vote, he said.
"If we see that there could be a political crisis over the rejection of the budget then we will abstain. If we abstain, this means the budget passes," he said in an interview on Monday night.

The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, which toppled the PSD from power in elections exactly one year ago, must present its budget plan to parliament before October 15. A vote is expected in November.

Rebelo de Sousa said that the PSD was as committed as the government, which is four seats short of an absolute majority in the 230-seat chamber, to seeing Portugal amongst the first wave of European Union countries to wed their economies in Economic and Monetary Union in January 1999.

The PSD wanted to see more decisive cuts in state spending than the government was likely to offer in its 1997 budget programme, he said, but a national election campaign next year could torpedo Portugal's chances of qualifying for the single currency, he said.
